purpose: Routing index for the dub, sub, wub and 808 literature that pop/dance/synths/wobble.mjs, skrill.mjs and the climbalift bed in pop/notespatial/ are specified against.
posture: Index and citation only. Tutorials are tutorials, forum threads are consensus, artist interviews are the artist. Nothing is mirrored into the repo.

checked_key.true: page fetched and the cited facts read from it during the 2026-09-25 platter pass
checked_key.false: cited from a search excerpt or a page that refused the fetch; wants a verification pass before it is cited in a paper

sources.title: The Roots of Dub
sources.author: Kirk Degiorgio, Red Bull Music Academy Daily
sources.note: Tubby's 1972 MCI 12-into-4 with per-channel reverb sends, the custom high-pass, the spring struck with a stick, tape delays, master compression.

sources.title: Dub Filter — King Tubby's High Pass
sources.author: AudioThing
sources.note: Altec 9069B: passive inductor T-network, 10 positions, 70 Hz–7.5 kHz, 18 dB/oct; the Big Knob.

sources.title: Dub music
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.note: Ruddy Redwood 1968, versions, Tubby/Perry/Scientist/Thompson, drop-outs, Space Echo, influence on jungle and dubstep.

sources.title: One drop rhythm
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.note: Kick and cross-stick on 3, beat 1 empty, bass rests on the one; rockers and steppers; audio examples at 80 BPM.

sources.title: King Tubby Meets Rockers Uptown (song)
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.note: 1974, Pablo/Tubby/Barrett, versions Jacob Miller; Veal's eighth-note bass over I minor–IV minor.

sources.title: Black Ark
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.note: 1973–79, four-track Soundcraft and TEAC, Echoplex and Space Echo, bouncing overdubs, Tubby designed the circuitry.

sources.title: Scientist (musician)
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.note: b. 1960; mixing at Tubby's four-track mid-1970s, 16-track at Channel One, Roots Radics.

sources.title: Roland RE-201
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.note: 1974, free-running tape loop, one record and three playback heads, spring reverb, Perry's use.

sources.title: Dub: Soundscapes and Shattered Songs in Jamaican Reggae
sources.author: Michael E. Veal, Wesleyan University Press
sources.note: The study of 1970s Jamaican engineers turning studio processing into composition; ARSC award 2008.

sources.title: Dub Mixing
sources.author: Andrea Terrano, Sound on Sound
sources.note: Real-time analogue mixing; delay about 0.7 s heard 4–5 times; feedback via return channel; filter and limit the return; bass sits high and militant.

sources.title: Beat Techniques: Dub Production
sources.author: zZounds Music Blog
sources.note: Drop-out technique: guitars/keys out for 2 bars leaving drums and bass, or the reverse, or swap. Page returned 403; cited from search excerpt.

sources.title: Trying to get this Reggae bass sound
sources.author: Gearspace forum
sources.note: Flatwounds, tone rolled off, near the neck, foam mute, DI with preamp/tube compressor; Barrett P-Bass, Shakespeare Fenders, early Höfners. Consensus, not an artist interview; page returned 403, cited from search excerpt.

sources.title: Dub techno
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.note: Berlin early 1990s, Basic Channel 1993, Rhythm & Sound, Chain Reaction; 110–125 BPM; delay and reverb; Deepchord, Vladislav Delay, Monolake.

sources.title: Basic Channel
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.note: von Oswald and Ernestus 1993; nine 12"s 1993–94; labels; Dubplates & Mastering; BCD 1995.

sources.title: Basic Channel-Style Dub Techno (Beat Dissected)
sources.author: Aykan Esen, Attack Magazine
sources.note: Chord band-pass ~450 Hz 12 dB, 6-bit, dotted-eighth echo, bass cut below ~37 Hz and sidechained fastest attack; session at 145 BPM.

sources.title: Dub Techno Synth Chords (Synth Secrets)
sources.author: Adam Douglas, Attack Magazine
sources.note: High-pass chord; taps at dotted eighth ~20% and 264 ms ~85%; send EQ HPF 100 Hz, LPF 4.5 kHz, −7 dB at 600 Hz; plate, phaser.

sources.title: DeepChord Doesn't Care About Your Fancy New Synthesizer
sources.author: Patrick Russell, Vice
sources.note: Processors over synths; Prophet VS and vintage FX; field recordings on cheap recorders; ASQ-10 and Linn 9000 sequencing.

sources.title: Deepchord (feature)
sources.author: Tom Durston, Inverted Audio
sources.note: "So little of the original signal remains"; field recordings made while something was happening; works at night.

sources.title: Dub Techno (Basic Channel, DeepChord, Echocord) HOWTO?
sources.author: KVR Audio forum
sources.note: Practitioner consensus: spring reverb model plus GS-201-type tape echo, tape saturation, evolving delay/reverb chains; Basic Channel never interviewed, Prophet-5 assumed.

sources.title: Mala (Digital Mystikz) — RBMA lecture, Barcelona
sources.author: Red Bull Music Academy
sources.note: Straight sine plus EQ; low-cut around 40 Hz; FWD>> rig at Plastic People; jungle as London dub; 138→140 BPM; DMZ 2004, first night March 2005; Reason from 2000.

sources.title: Skream — RBMA lecture, Melbourne
sources.author: Red Bull Music Academy
sources.note: "You can make a bass from anything ... They're just tones"; cut at 30 Hz not 40 for systems reaching 20 Hz; FruityLoops; Midnight Request Line origin; heaviness is the bass.

sources.title: A Space for Bass: Loefah
sources.author: Raz Mesinai, Underground PA (Substack)
sources.note: The delayed drop, spacing between hits, sub tuned for systems and headphones, DMZ and Swamp 81.

sources.title: Dubstep Basics
sources.author: Peter Jenkins, Sound on Sound
sources.note: ~140 BPM half-time; sine sub with fundamental ~30–60 Hz (article says C0–C1; see digest Debts); sidechain sub to kick or hat; mono legato; cut don't boost; sine LFO smoother.

sources.title: Dubstep Secrets
sources.author: Geoff Smith, Sound on Sound
sources.note: Oscillators at −24/−12 played C2–C3; FM edge; 24 dB LPF with LFO 2 at synced 1/8; mono; 570 ms release; sine at fundamental; parallel distortion.

sources.title: Dubstep
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.note: Name 2001/2002; FWD>> and DMZ; 132–142 BPM, 140 common; snare every third beat; minor/Phrygian; wobble as LFO-modulated synth; Skrillex and brostep; riddim.

sources.title: Wobble Bass Guide
sources.author: Rendr with Deadly Habit and Macc, Dubstepforum
sources.note: LFO to low-pass; start at 1/8; LFO shapes; sub is a 40–50 Hz sine with LFO on amplitude since a low-pass does nothing to a sine.

sources.title: Mixing Bass
sources.author: Mike Senior, Sound on Sound
sources.note: Phase-coherent below 100 Hz for PA mono sums; HPF secondary layers ~100 Hz; sines/triangles on-off envelope; duck 2–3 dB per kick; kick in 100–200 Hz if bass owns sub-40; 1 kHz lift; parallel distortion LPF 2–3 kHz, phase-checked.

sources.title: Center That Sub! (A Guide to Monoing Your Low End)
sources.author: Ian Stewart, Flotown Mastering
sources.note: Mono below ~100–200 Hz; vinyl and single-sub PA reasons; linear-phase or first-order filters; avoid steep minimum-phase.

sources.title: MONO bass — when Mastering For VINYL
sources.author: Masterdisk
sources.note: Elliptical EQ crossover 75–300 Hz, 150 Hz common; vertical groove excursion limits level and tracking. Cited from search excerpt; page not fetched.

sources.title: Sub-bass
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.note: Below ~70 Hz to 20 Hz, felt more than heard; piano A0 27.5 Hz; bass E 41.2 Hz; dubstep bass lines mainly sub-bass.

sources.title: Missing fundamental
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.note: Virtual pitch from harmonics; telephones pass little under 300 Hz yet 150 Hz voices keep pitch; MaxxBass 1999 synthesises harmonics above a speaker's cutoff.

sources.title: How to Make Bass Audible on Phone Speakers
sources.author: Alex Lavoie, LANDR Blog
sources.note: Phones filter below 200 Hz, nothing under 100; 250–700 Hz carries the note; multiband drive 700 Hz–1.5 kHz; octave-up layer; mono; HPF returns 200–400 Hz.

sources.title: Reese bass
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.note: Saunderson 1988 "Just Want Another Chance", Casio CZ-1000 phase distortion; jungle/DnB uses 1994–98; into dubstep.

sources.title: Phase distortion synthesis
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.note: Casio 1984, CZ series; piecewise-linear modulators locked to the cycle; flatter spectra than FM; windowed-sine resonance.

sources.title: How to build an LFO wobble bass
sources.author: Roland Schmidt, MusicRadar
sources.note: Wobble as the sound that "captured the production psyche"; Skrillex named; mid-80s Roland LFO button precedent. General, few numbers; listed for context.

sources.title: Q&A: Caspa & Rusko
sources.author: Vivian Host, XLR8R
sources.note: Caspa: Reason only, "LFOs and basslines"; Rusko: Acid, drums, melodies and chords; dubplates for "bassy, loud, and crispy".

sources.title: Rusko (musician)
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.note: b. 1985, Leeds Sub Dub, Sub Soldiers with Caspa; FabricLive.37 (2007), Cockney Thug (2009), Woo Boost (2010).

sources.title: War of the Wubs: The Strange and Contentious History of Dubstep
sources.author: Crossfadr
sources.note: Wobble arrives later, subtle with Skream/Silkie; Rusko credited with the harsher tone; Skrillex fixes "loud, lurching and aggressive"; the "autotune of this decade" quote.

sources.title: Scary Monsters and Nice Sprites (song)
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.note: 22 Oct 2010, 140 BPM, B♭; began as "FM8 Test" after Noisia's Nik showed Skrillex FM8; Grammy 2012; popularised "the drop".

sources.title: Skrillex Bass Tutorial — Create A Skrillex Growl Bass Sound Using FM8
sources.author: Dan Larsson, Loopmasters
sources.note: FM8 in Ableton through Ohmicide, two auto-filters, a WOW filter, overdrive, EQ, limiter. Settings are in the video, not the page.

sources.title: MASSIVE Manual — Oscillator Section
sources.author: Native Instruments
sources.note: Three wavetable oscillators; Wt-Position scans the table; Intensity modes Spectrum, three Bend modes, Formant ("morphing vowels").

sources.title: Serum Manual
sources.author: Xfer Records (Steve Duda)
sources.note: LFO Rate 0–20 Hz free, snaps to note values down to 1/32 when BPM-synced; Trig mode restarts per note. PDF not text-extractable at fetch; figures confirmed against a tutorial summary (EDMProd).

sources.title: Twisted Neuro Bass (Synth Secrets)
sources.author: Attack Magazine
sources.note: Massive: two wavetables, one −24 with Bend; noise 33%; band-reject ~25%; glide 66%; LFO synced 1/1 to WT position (33%, opposite) and cutoff (50%); tube 60/90; freq shifter; 1/16 shelf wobble; mono legato.

sources.title: Learn How To Make Noisia-Inspired Synths With Ableton's Operator
sources.author: Attack Magazine
sources.note: 174 BPM; FM from B at +17 st; 65 ms attack; −38 st pitch; Erosion→EQ→425 ms reverb 12% 35% stereo→OTT 45%→Saturator; layer OTT 100%; bus Saturator +10→OTT 50%→limiter.

sources.title: Noisia
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.note: Groningen 2003; Roos, van Sonderen, de Vlieger; Split the Atom 2010, Outer Edges 2016, Closer 2022; final show 2022.

sources.title: Neurofunk
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.note: From techstep mid–late 1990s; Reynolds, The Wire Dec 1997; Ed Rush & Optical Wormhole 1998; wavetable/FM basses with moving mids over constant low weight; Noisia, Phace, Mefjus.

sources.title: OTT By Xfer Records: Free Multiband Compressor For Any DAW
sources.author: Mike Thornton, Production Expert
sources.note: Three-band upward and downward compressor; from an Ableton Multiband Dynamics preset; Depth, Time, In, Out.

sources.title: Virtual Riot Interview — Producing Dubstep and Bass Music
sources.author: Antares
sources.note: Two-hour knob-twisting recordings chopped and reloaded as wavetables and sampler material; loud and compressed while keeping dynamics. Page returned 503; cited from search excerpt.

sources.title: How to Make Dubstep Bass in Serum
sources.author: Preset Drive
sources.note: LFO rates 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16; WT-pos depth 50%/20–30%; riddim WT change every other bar; FM ~30% from +1 oct; notch and MG filters; res 40–50%; chains (hard clip 40–50%, sine fold, downsample); EQ→dist→OTT→EQ→limiter −1 dB; cut mid below 80–100 Hz; pitch +12→0 in ~30 ms; 0 ms attack, 300–400 ms decay.

sources.title: Riddim (genre)
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.note: Croydon early 2010s, mainstream ~2015; minimal repetitive sub-bass and triplet percussion at 140–150; Jakes, Subfiltronik, Infekt; LFO squares, wide delays, flanger/chorus.

sources.title: Infekt's Guide To Riddim
sources.author: UKF
sources.note: Subfiltronik, DJ Shiverz, Coffi 2012–13 as blueprint; space, reverb, dark textures, repetition, flow; 140, 150 a different vibe.

sources.title: What is Riddim Dubstep? The Minimalistic Bass-Heavy Subgenre
sources.author: BassGorilla
sources.note: Layering, LFO/envelope modulation, distortion, resampling; arrangement; Subfiltronik/Deemed/Infekt tracks; gives 130–135 BPM, which contradicts Wikipedia and Infekt.

sources.title: Ten Tips For Better Basslines (tip 4, sidechain)
sources.author: Bruce Aisher, Attack Magazine
sources.note: Up to 6 dB of kick-triggered compression before obvious pumping; fastest attack short of clicks; release to kick decay and tempo.

sources.title: Sidechain Compression: The Complete Guide
sources.author: Tyler Connaghan, eMastered
sources.note: 2:1, attack ≤2 ms, release <50 ms subtle, 2–3 dB; for dance time the release to the track, quarter = 60000/BPM ms; HPF the sidechain ~100 Hz on a bus.

sources.title: Mixing 808 bass: fat, clean, and audible on every speaker
sources.author: Chris Jones, Peak Studios
sources.note: Core 30–60 Hz, gone below ~28 Hz; phones struggle under 200 Hz; mono below ~120 Hz; parallel distortion high-cut 150 Hz into a 200–400 Hz band; 40→80/120/160 Hz harmonics; kick sidechain short and fast. Undated page.

sources.title: How to Make 808s in FL Studio: From Scratch to Battle-Ready
sources.author: Audeobox Learn
sources.note: Roots C1–G1 (32–49 Hz); attack 0, decay 3–5 s, sustain 0, release 100–200 ms; 1–2 st drop over 10–30 ms; glide; soft clip −3 to −6 dB; 5–15% FM; LPF 500–800 Hz on drive; HPF 20–25 Hz; peaks −6 to −3; 2:1–4:1; mono below 200 Hz.

sources.title: Roland TR-808
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.note: 1980–83, ~12,000 units; bass drum = sine oscillator, low-pass, VCA with decay control; Rick Rubin lengthened decay and tuned it into bass lines; Southern hip-hop and trap.

sources.title: Chopped and screwed
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.note: DJ Screw, Houston, late 1980s; slowed to 60–70 BPM with pitch; skips, scratches, stop-time; seeded witch house, vaporwave, cloud rap, phonk.

sources.title: Witch house (genre)
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.note: Salem (2006); name coined Dec 2009 by Pictureplane; drum machines, trap loops, heavily layered basslines, dense reverb, pitched-down vocals, screwed tempo, industrial/drone.

sources.title: Bewitched: Salem Interviewed
sources.author: John Doran, The Quietus
sources.note: Holland: "it's a good idea to slow down any music, not just rap music"; Houston screw and Memphis influence; no demo stage.

sources.title: Salem: 808s and heartache
sources.author: Chris Powers, FACT Magazine
sources.note: King Night as chopped-and-screwed hip-hop with stripped drum machines; 808-fuelled Redlights remix; distortion as another layer; Jack builds the beat first.

sources.title: Cloud rap
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.note: Late 2000s; Lil B, Clams Casino; term 2010; A$AP Rocky "Peso" 2011; Yung Lean "Ginseng Strip 2002" 2013; Drain Gang; reverb-heavy ethereal chopped samples.

sources.title: Whitearmor: 'Everything I've ever wanted to say has been in the melodies'
sources.author: Günseli Yalcinkaya, Dazed
sources.note: Melody-first; problem-based mindset; blog-era and Atlanta rap influences; no gear or 808 technique given.

sources.title: Interview: Yung Gud
sources.author: Max Bell, Red Bull Music Academy Daily
sources.note: GarageBand to Ableton Live 9; psytrance at twelve; Lex Luger and Actress; atmospheric low-end-heavy hip-hop; no mixing specifics.
